## Highlights since 0.20.2

- **Antigravity joins the Agent's providers.** The bundled Agent runtime moves to Synara 1.6.8, which runs Antigravity (`agy`) over ACP like the other agent CLIs, so it gets Lattice's tools, approvals, questions and its quota under Usage & limits. A signed-out `agy` shows as not signed in, with a Sign in button that starts only when you click it. Antigravity models can also be chosen for Proofread, Polish, annotation revisions and Git writing; those tasks run read-only and never start a sign-in on their own.
- **Write an Overleaf comment beside its passage.** In the native Lattice, Comment on Overleaf in the source editor's selection toolbar opens a small composer beside the selection instead of the Overleaf panel, so the sentence stays in view while you write. ⌘↵ sends it and puts you back in the text with the passage selected. While the file isn't live, the composer says why and Send waits; a refused send keeps your text and shows the error.
- **Overleaf comment markers stay on their own passage.** In the native Lattice, cutting or deleting a commented passage no longer moves its marker onto the text that follows. The thread is detached, as on Overleaf, and the Comments panel lists it as "(this comment's text was removed)". Undo, or pasting the same text back in place, re-attaches the thread on Overleaf, as Overleaf's own editor does.
- **Annotation revisions read the paper around a section file.** In the native Lattice, when a paper is split into section files under its main document, a revision now also gives the Agent the main document's preamble (its macros, notation and theorem environments), and, near the start or end of a file, the text TeX reads just before or after it. The Agent still revises only the annotated passage.

## Notable fixes

- Lists in embedded Agent settings, such as the Proofreading model list, scroll with the mouse wheel and trackpad, and their popups stay inside the visible part of the Settings sheet (#1379).
- In the native Lattice, the title bar's Overleaf dot turns amber while Overleaf's "too many requests" cool-down runs, instead of looking online, and live sync no longer sends an extra check right after the connection comes back.
- In the native Lattice, the PDF menu's Export review PDF… waits until the PDF on screen can be annotated, so it no longer opens a sheet that places no notes right after a build.
- In the native Lattice, after you stop a build, automatic builds of the same files wait until you change one, so a document that loops is not built again on its own.
- Help › Report a Problem… names the operating system and its version, such as Windows 10.0.26100 or Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, instead of "macOS unknown" on Windows and Linux.
- On Linux, LaTeX builds with Ubuntu 22.04's latexmk 4.76 report their errors, hidden builds keep their files out of the document's folder, and a broken document built again unchanged is no longer reported as built.
